view: This print turns on the Q4/FY guide and the Glob.AI ARR trajectory, not on Q3. Q3 was guided to a decline and consensus sits at the guide midpoint. Globant has landed at or above its quarterly guide recently (Q1 2026 beat its guide; Q2 came in at $614.4M against $610-616M), so a small Q3 revenue beat is the base case and carries little. The risk is Q4. A flat-demand Globant ran Q4 below Q3 last year (Q4 2025 $612.6M against Q3 2025 $617.1M, -0.7%; own arithmetic from the guide percentages). Q3 near $613M with the same seasonality points to a Q4 guide midpoint around $605-610M, a hair under the $610M consensus. That would narrow FY to the lower half, roughly in line with the $5.91 FY EPS consensus, which already sits in the lower half of the range. Two specific soft spots, the video-game client (Guggenheim, Nov 11) and the Middle East (about 4% of revenue, already cut in August), are named in public and partly in the price after the downgrade day. Against that, positioning is extreme: 26% of float short, 10+ days to cover, a 6.5x multiple, and a stock that has just fallen 11% with the sector on no company news. The two prints since Feb that did not cut the FY guide gapped +2% and +10%. My net read: a modest Q4 shortfall against consensus is somewhat more likely than not, and the crowded short and the washed-out tape mean an in-line guide gets bought. Those offset, and I cannot see the deciding line well enough to lean more than a couple of points. No edge worth a recommendation.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line is the Q4 guide against a $610M consensus that already sits at the implied midpoint of the August guide. Seasonality and Globant's habit of guiding forward periods below consensus (5 of the last 7 prints) lean slightly negative. A 26% short interest and a sector-driven 11% run-down into the print lean the other way on the reaction. Neither side has dated company-specific evidence the price clearly lacks.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 guide midpoint at or above about $612M with FY held or narrowed to the midpoint, plus Glob.AI ARR in the high-$70Ms or better for September, would likely set off a sharp squeeze given 26% of float short. A Q4 guide under $600M or a further FY cut would make it a clear down gap.

self_critique: The case for a bigger lean down: Globant has guided forward periods below consensus on most recent prints, Cognizant's bookings fell and Accenture/Infosys flagged AI price deflation, and a known large-client risk was flagged a week ago, so Q4 could come in well under $600M and the FY could be cut again (as in August, -6.8% at the open). The case for up: the short is at a record level, the multiple is 6.5x, the sector just washed out, the closest peer (EPAM) beat and raised, and an in-line guide with strong ARR could gap +10% as in May. Both are plausible, and that is why I stay near 50.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition helped most here: it showed the 12% fall was the sector and the tape, not company news. P7's 'estimate the line from its inputs' gave only a weak lean, because the consensus had already been reset to the guide. The playbook has no guidance on weighing a guide-below-consensus habit against an extreme short base when both are in plain view.
